title: Repeated evidence reaches a limit
lesson: Record comparable observations from a fixed test selection; a configured limit on repeated failure evidence stops edits and hands the trace to an engineer. Passing tests also exit to human review.

transcript.text: The agent sends EDIT 1 around the ring to a fixed 12-test suite. Five tests fail; 5 FAIL enters the run log with a full illustrative bar.
EDIT 2 returns 2 FAIL under the same selection. A shorter bar and a check mark register the reduced count. Counts summarize this example; they are not a sufficient general progress test.
EDIT 3 returns PASS. The log retains the earlier observations, a REVIEW badge appears, the loop dims, and a REVIEW chip reaches the human for patch review.

The scene fades into a separate task with a repeat limit of three. Its first edit returns FAIL a7; the log records 3 FAIL · a7. Here a7 represents one normalized assertion report, not merely a failure count.
The second edit returns the same report a7. Two matching log entries turn amber and a warning mark appears.
The third edit returns a7 again. Three matching entries reach this example’s configured repeat limit: the log turns red, a REPEAT LIMIT badge appears, and the agent and loop dim.
HAND OFF travels from the retained run log to the human. The human lights to acknowledge receipt; the blocker has not been repaired. The resolved handoff holds before a full-frame fade.

limitations: The repeat threshold of three is an illustrative policy, not an optimal count or proof that a repair is impossible.

The same failure count can hide different failing tests. The revised repeated-report identifier a7 stands for matching failure identities and relevant assertion details under a fixed selection; it is not a suggested production hash length.
The initial falling-count example assumes stable tests and controlled state; counts or a single green run alone do not prove overall correctness.
The run log represents executable harness checks; the animation does not demonstrate permission enforcement or timeout cancellation.
Iteration budgets are complementary and shown in the baseline cut.
Audio was analysed by signal levels, cue windows and spectrogram, not heard.
Original author provenance is retained; teaching and render corrections are attributed separately.

changes: Replaced the unsupported equal-count/no-progress inference with a configured repeat limit over matching failure reports (a7); retained the three-failure observations.
Bound observations to a fixed 12-test suite, enlarged log/chip text, and added a success review handoff.
Fade the entire frame at loop boundaries.
Replaced long primary-source quotations with concise paraphrases and links.
